draft.title: Locating points in three dimensions
card: In three dimensions there are three axes at right angles to each other: x, y and z. They meet at the origin, (0, 0, 0).
A point is written as (x, y, z). The numbers give the distance along each axis, in that order.
To find (3, 2, 4), move 3 along the x axis, then 2 along the y axis, then 4 up the z axis.
A negative number means you move the opposite way along that axis. A zero means you do not move along it.
draft.remember: A point in space needs three coordinates, (x, y, z), one for each axis.

a.q: In the point (5, 1, 8), what does the 8 tell you?
opts: The distance along the z axis
The distance along the x axis
The distance along the y axis
a.why: The third number is the z coordinate, so 8 is the distance along the z axis. It is not the distance from the origin, which would need all three numbers.
a.clue: The order is x, y, z.

b.q: A drone starts at the origin and moves to the point (4, 0, 6). Which describes its path?
opts: 4 along x, none along y, 6 up z
4 along y, none along x, 6 up z
4 along x, 6 along y, none up z
None along x, 4 along y, 6 up z
b.why: The coordinates are (x, y, z), so x is 4, y is 0 and z is 6. The drone moves 4 along x, does not move along y, and rises 6 up z. Swapping x and y is a common order mistake.
b.clue: A zero means no movement along that axis.

a.best: The distance along the z axis

b.best: 4 along x, none along y, 6 up z
